reason: A volunteer gains. One clock replaces two: silence for 24 hours makes the application complete, 48 hours makes it granted, so a slow Commission cannot stall a minor party. The single incompleteness notice, confined to s 8.5(2), ends drip-fed delay, and relation-back preserves the five-working-day lead time a correction would otherwise burn. The 24-hour cure is tight for someone in paid work, and the one-occasion rule shifts residual risk to applicants, but indefinite delay was worse. Takedown exposure attaches only to prescribed techniques, not ordinary self-certified advertising.
conditions: Extend the s 8.5(7) correction window to two working days, or provide that a correction completed before the s 8.5(1) lead time expires keeps the original receipt date, and require the incompleteness notice by email and text to the contact named in the application, so a volunteer in paid work is not timed out.
